# China City Explorer - Full Content Index

## Summary

China City Explorer helps travelers choose and connect Chinese cities. It combines city guides, comparison pages, high-speed rail routes, and month-by-month recommendations.

## City Database

Beijing (3 days, $65-120/day): First-time visitors who want imperial history and iconic landmarks. Best months: Apr, May, Sep, Oct. If you can only visit one city, make it Beijing.

Shanghai (3 days, $70-130/day): A polished city break with strong food and design. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Best single-city trip for a short, comfortable, food-driven stay.

Xi'an (2 days, $50-95/day): Terracotta Army and the Ming city wall. Best months: Apr, May, Sep, Oct. Best second city for a first China trip.

Chengdu (3 days, $45-85/day): Pandas, teahouses, and serious Sichuan food. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Sep, Oct. Best relaxed city and gateway to Tibet and western China.

Chongqing (2 days, $45-80/day): Night photography, dramatic urban landscapes, and hotpot. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Must for photographers and hotpot fans; pair with Chengdu.

Guilin (2 days, $45-80/day): Accessible karst scenery and the Li River. Best months: Apr, May, Sep, Oct. Best three-day nature break in southern China with Yangshuo.

Yangshuo (2 days, $40-75/day): Cycling, river scenery, and rural bases near Guilin. Best months: Apr, May, Sep, Oct. Do not skip Yangshuo when visiting Guilin.

Hangzhou (2 days, $55-100/day): West Lake and Longjing tea villages. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Best two-day green escape from Shanghai.

Suzhou (2 days, $50-90/day): Classical gardens and canals. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Best garden city and ideal second stop on a Shanghai-Hangzhou loop.

Nanjing (2 days, $50-90/day): Layered history and strong museums. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Best underrated stop between Beijing and Shanghai.

Harbin (2 days, $45-85/day): Ice and Snow World and Russian-influenced architecture. Best months: Dec, Jan, Feb. Single best winter city in China.

Kunming (2 days, $40-75/day): Mild weather and the gateway to Yunnan. Best months: Mar, Apr, May, Oct, Nov. Best starting point for a Yunnan trip.

Lhasa (3 days, $70-130/day): Tibetan culture, Potala Palace, and Jokhang Temple. Best months: May, Jun, Sep, Oct. Bucket-list trip; plan for altitude and permits.

Hong Kong (3 days, $85-160/day): Skyline, dim sum, shopping, and island escapes. Best months: Oct, Nov, Dec, Mar, Apr. Best soft landing for nervous first-timers.

Zhangjiajie (2 days, $55-95/day): Sandstone pillars and forest views. Best months: Apr, May, Sep, Oct. Top-tier nature destination for photographers.

## Routes

7-day classic triangle: Beijing, Xi'an, Chengdu. Beijing 3 days, Xi'an 2 days, Chengdu 2 days. $600-900 per person. About 8 hours of rail. Best for first-timers who want history, food, and pandas.

10-day Jiangnan loop: Shanghai, Suzhou, Hangzhou. Shanghai 3 days, Suzhou 2 days, Hangzhou 2 days, back to Shanghai 1 day. $850-1,200 per person. Under 3 hours of rail. Best for design, food, gardens, and minimal transit.

14-day panorama: Beijing, Xi'an, Chengdu, Guilin, Hong Kong. Beijing 3, Xi'an 2, Chengdu 2, Guilin 2, Hong Kong 3 days. $1,400-2,000 per person. About 12 hours of rail plus 2 flights. Best for a broad first pass across regions.

## Month Guidance

January: Harbin, Beijing, Hong Kong. Best for ice festivals and indoor city culture. Avoid northern cities outside Harbin unless you want deep cold.

February: Harbin, Shanghai, Kunming. Colder in the north, milder in the south. Avoid the Spring Festival travel rush; book trains early.

March: Shanghai, Hangzhou, Chengdu. Spring starts, gardens and tea villages open up. Avoid Beijing during spring dust storms.

April: Beijing, Suzhou, Guilin. Pleasant temperatures and strong spring scenery. Avoid the Qingming holiday weekend for crowds.

May: Xi'an, Chengdu, Zhangjiajie. Green mountains and good walking weather. Avoid the Labor Day holiday week.

June: Kunming, Guilin, Hong Kong. Rainy season begins. Avoid southern cities if you dislike rain.

July: Kunming, Lhasa, Harbin. Head to higher altitude or cooler northern cities. Avoid lowland cities in peak heat.

August: Lhasa, Kunming, Harbin. Peak summer travel and domestic holidays. Avoid the south during typhoon season.

September: Beijing, Xi'an, Chengdu. Comfortable weather after the summer peak. Avoid the Mid-Autumn holiday weekend.

October: Beijing, Guilin, Hangzhou. Golden autumn light and holiday crowds. Avoid the first week.

November: Shanghai, Suzhou, Hong Kong. Lower crowds and cooler city walking. Avoid northern cities as temperatures drop.

December: Harbin, Hong Kong, Shanghai. Ice season in the north, mild city breaks in the south. Avoid the far north unless you want the ice festival.

## Practical Notes

Most visitors need an L visa, but visa-free transit and regional waivers change often. Set up Alipay or WeChat Pay with an international card. Google, WhatsApp, and many Western apps are blocked, so install a VPN before arrival if needed. Use Apple Maps, Amap, or Baidu Maps instead of Google Maps. Book high-speed rail on China Railway 12306 or a trusted service, and book major attractions 1-2 weeks ahead.
